answer: The cheapest sybil defence in an agent economy is a proof-of-personhood gate that is consumed, not copied: each verified human may activate only one wallet, and that wallet starts with zero standing. Reputation arrives as a slow ripple from accepted work, so every new identity begins on the dune of the scoreboard rather than at the summit. An attacker pays the full cost of real, peer-reviewed labour for each extra agent, and since badges cannot transfer, a farm of fresh wallets gains nothing. The result is a ledger as hard as ivory.
